text:
rachel: Quick probe — proposing we move the "slowpath requeue" responsibility out of upstream services and into the edge gateway. RFC draft: https://redwood.internal/rfc/edge-requeue (WIP). TL;DR: when ingress detects a streaming stall or upstream stall > 350ms, the edge enqueues a requeue attempt to a healthy backend while keeping the client stream alive. Pros: reduces upstream memory pressure and prevents long-tail single-host hotspots. Cons: introduces duplicate/ordering risk and KV-warmup costs for LLM backends.

tomas: how do we avoid duplicate side-effects? most services aren't idempotent by default, we need a clear dedupe mechanism.

maria: we have an existing idempotency header (x-rw-id) but lots of customers don't set it for streaming requests. fingerprinting request body+offset could work but is expensive for large contexts.

evan: edge can attach a generated requeue token header (x-rw-requeue) and short-live lease metadata. Upstreams that opt-in can dedupe within a 5s window. Fallback for legacy services: hedging + rate cap.

rachel: proto sketch: header `x-rw-requeue: <uuid>`; edge stores tiny requeue-index (uuid -> origin-session) for ~2s. On requeue, edge sends `x-rw-requeue` to candidate upstream and emits trace spans. If upstream sees duplicate it should return 409 with `x-rw-requeue-dup: true`.

sajid: KV cache concern — detaching midstream means new upstream has cold KV; for generation-heavy models the warmup token cost dominates latency. We could avoid switching for LLM models unless upstream advertises cold-warm swap support.

maria: +1. Other idea: edge shadow-warm the candidate upstream (fanout the prefix to warm KV) before switch, but that doubles tokens and costs. Maybe do it only for high-value sessions.

anna: observability needs: `edge.requeue.count`, `edge.requeue.latency`, `edge.requeue.outcome` (success/dup/fallback). Must sample full traces for midflight switches to debug context loss.

evan: also we should cap requeues to 1 per request to avoid loops and cascading requeues. implement global per-conn budget.

tomas: memory at edge: storing per-inflight requeue metadata increases p99 mem a bit; we need admission control and compact encoding (store only uuid + 16B).

rachel: proposed rollout: feature-flagged experiment (edge.requeue off by default). Phase 1: opt-in Canary with only idempotent endpoints. Phase 2: add KV-aware heuristics and opt-in header for upstreams to opt into warm-pointer swaps. I'll write a follow-up RFC with state machine, exact header contract, failure modes, and a small perf experiment plan. @eng-runtime @sre please take a look.

deploy-bot: Feature flag `edge.requeue` created (off).

eng-runtime: reading — quick request: include a small compatibility table in the RFC (models that must avoid requeue vs safe hedging).

sre: watchlist: add an alert if `edge.requeue.outcome{fallback}` > 0.5% over 10m. Also add a burn-rate detector for requeue token spikes.

rachel: thanks — will incorporate. plan to submit RFC by EOD tomorrow and a tiny canary toggle next week.
